methodologyNotes: Specs sourced from manufacturer spec pages, Wikipedia hardware articles, and corroborating reputable tech sources. display_per_eye is the panel resolution in pixels per eye (width x height). refresh_hz is the maximum supported refresh rate in Hz. fov_deg is the horizontal field of view in degrees (diagonal where only diagonal is published). tracking describes the tracking modality. standalone is true when the headset operates without a tethered PC or console. storage_gb is the base/lowest configuration in gigabytes; null when no internal storage (PC-tethered headsets). weight_g is headset weight in grams (excluding external battery packs where noted). passthrough is true when the headset has cameras enabling view of the real world. release is the calendar year-month of US/global commercial availability. priceUsd is the US MSRP for the base configuration noted in priceNote; null when the product has no official US retail price. accessedAt is 2026-06-15 on all sources. A null is used only for genuinely unknown values, never as a guess.

products.name: Meta Quest 3
products.priceNote: US MSRP for 128 GB base config as of Sept 2024 price reduction; 512 GB is $499
products.provenance: Wikipedia Meta Quest 3: 2064x2208 per eye RGB-stripe LCD+, 90-120 Hz, 515 g, 128 GB and 512 GB models, inside-out optical SLAM. FOV ~110° horizontal confirmed via multiple review sources (improved from Quest 2's 97°). Color passthrough (4 MP RGB camera). Released October 10, 2023. Price reduced to $429.99 / $499.99 in September 2024 when Quest 3S launched.

products.name: Meta Quest 3S
products.priceNote: US MSRP for 128 GB base config; 256 GB is $399
products.provenance: Wikipedia Meta Quest 3S: 1832x1920 per eye, 90-120 Hz, 514 g, 128 GB and 256 GB models, Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2, Fresnel lenses, 96° horizontal FOV (narrower than Quest 3's 110°), color passthrough cameras. Released October 15, 2024 at $299.99 (128 GB) / $399.99 (256 GB).

products.name: Apple Vision Pro (M5)
products.priceNote: US starting MSRP for 256 GB; 512 GB and 1 TB configurations available at higher prices

specs.tracking: inside-out (6 world cameras + 4 eye-tracking cameras + 4 IMUs)

products.provenance: Wikipedia Apple Vision Pro: M5 variant released October 22, 2025. ~3660x3200 per eye micro-OLED (23M pixels total), up to 120 Hz. FOV ~100°x73° (horizontal ~100° used for fov_deg). Weight 750-800 g for M5 headset (midpoint 775 g; excludes 353 g external battery). Storage 256 GB / 512 GB / 1 TB. Standalone via Apple M5 + R1 chip. Full passthrough via 12 cameras including stereoscopic 3D main camera. US price $3,499 unchanged from M2 launch. Apple specs page corroborates display, refresh rates, and storage.

products.priceNote: US launch MSRP; headset only (requires PS5 or PC via adapter)

specs.tracking: inside-out (4 headset cameras + IR eye tracking)

No internal storage (tethered to PS5 via USB-C; PC adapter released later). See-through passthrough function. Released February 22, 2023 at $549.99. products.name: Pico 4 Ultra
products.priceNote: Not sold in the United States; EU launch price was €549

products.name: Valve Index
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP for headset only; discontinued November 2025
products.provenance: Wikipedia Valve Index: 1440x1600 per eye LCD (full RGB), 80/90/120/144 Hz, estimated FOV ~108°, SteamVR Lighthouse 2.0 outside-in tracking, PC-tethered (DisplayPort 1.2 + USB 3.0), stereo RGB passthrough cameras (960x960 global shutter). US launch price $999. Discontinued November 12, 2025 (succeeded by Steam Frame). Headset-only weight 809 g (without cable) is consistently measured/reported across VRcompare and review outlets (Valve's own spec page omits it); ~888 g with cable. Valve headset page corroborates display and refresh specs.

products.name: HTC Vive XR Elite
products.provenance: Wikipedia HTC Vive XR Elite: 1920x1920 per eye, 90 Hz, up to 110° FOV, 625 g (with battery), 128 GB storage, Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2, inside-out tracking with 4 wide-FOV cameras + depth sensor, full-color RGB passthrough. Standalone capable; also connects to PC. Released February 2023 at $1,099. HTC Vive overview page corroborates standalone capability and passthrough.

products.name: HTC Vive Focus Vision
products.priceNote: US MSRP for Consumer Edition (128 GB); Business Edition is $1,299
products.provenance: Focus Vision unveiled September 2024: 2448x2448 per eye, 90 Hz (up to 120 Hz via DisplayPort), 120° FOV, 12 GB RAM, 128 GB storage (microSD expandable), 785 g, 16 MP color passthrough cameras, foveated rendering, eye/hand tracking, inside-out tracking. Standalone (also PC VR via DisplayPort). US Consumer Edition MSRP $999 (Engadget; sold by HTC and major US retailers B&H, Newegg, Adorama, Walmart); Business Edition $1,299. Earlier null for price/storage/weight corrected: all are confirmed via HTC official US store and reviews.

products.name: Pimax Crystal Super
products.priceNote: US price $1,783 USD for the Crystal Super QLED (57/50 PPD) configuration, cited verbatim ("At $1,783 USD, the Pimax Crystal Super commands a serious premium") in Boosted Media's detailed review. Pimax's own store surfaced only a EUR figure (€1,459) in the fetched locale, not a USD MSRP; includes optical engine plus two controllers.

specs.tracking: inside-out SLAM (4 tracking cameras; optional Lighthouse faceplate)

products.provenance: Pimax's official Crystal Super page confirms the exact model — a PCVR-only, interchangeable-optical-engine headset — with a spec table stating "Resolution : 3840x3840x2", "Refresh Rate : 72Hz/90Hz", and per-engine horizontal FOV ("FOV : 106°" for the 57PPD QLED, "FOV : 120°" for the 50PPD QLED recorded here, and up to 140° with the Ultrawide engine); its FAQ states the headset "always needs to be connected by its DP cable" (standalone=false, no battery, no internal storage). Boosted Media's detailed review of this same Crystal Super QLED cites the US price "$1,783 USD" (used for priceUsd) and independently confirms the 3840×3840-per-eye panel, SLAM tracking with four cameras, and a 127° FOV on the 50PPD version (Pimax's own spec table lists 120°, the value recorded to stay verbatim to the manufacturer). Pimax publishes no official weight and reviewer measurements conflict by audio-module/tether configuration (942 g with SMAS, 966 g and 1038 g with DMAS), so weight_g is null; releaseDate is null because a 2025 launch is only indicated by third-party reviews, not by the cited manufacturer or corroboration pages, and passthrough is null because neither fetched page states a passthrough view.

products.name: Varjo XR-4
products.priceNote: Road to VR spec table (Nov 27, 2023): XR-4 standard edition "priced at $4,000" (headset only, 33 PPD passthrough); the Focal Edition is $10,000 and Secure Editions $8,000/$14,000. Enterprise/simulation product requiring a Windows PC with NVIDIA GPU; not sold via consumer retail.

specs.tracking: inside-out (6 tracking cameras + LiDAR depth; optional SteamVR base stations)

products.provenance: Varjo's official XR-4 Series product page confirms the base XR-4: 3840 x 3744 per-eye mini-LED displays, 120° × 105° FOV, 200 hertz eye tracking, dual 20 MP passthrough cameras, inside-out plus optional SteamVR tracking, and PC-tethered operation (Windows + NVIDIA GPU, so not standalone; no internal storage). Road to VR's dated announcement/spec article (Nov 27, 2023) corroborates the 90Hz refresh rate and 665g headset weight, and explicitly separates the $4,000 standard XR-4 (33 PPD passthrough) from the $10,000 Focal Edition (51 PPD auto-focus), confirming this entry is the base XR-4 and not the Focal or Secure variant. Road to VR states the XR-4 "will begin shipping by the end of 2023," which sets release to 2023-12.

products.name: Shiftall MeganeX superlight 8K
products.priceNote: US MSRP $1,899 for the headset only (SteamVR base stations and controllers sold separately). Sourced verbatim from the Shiftall official product page Specification table ("Price $1,899") and the "US:$1,899" line; Road to VR's spec table also lists "Price $1,899" (its prose rounds to "$1,900").
products.provenance: The Shiftall official product page (en.shiftall.net/products/meganex8k, part no. SVP-VGC3B) confirms this exact model as the "MeganeX superlight 8K": 1.35-inch micro OLED at 3552 x 3840 per eye, 90 Hz, 179 g (main body only), 6DoF SteamVR Lighthouse tracking requiring base station 1.0/2.0 (explicitly "does not support inside-out tracking"), PC-tethered via DisplayPort + USB 2.0 (not standalone), and no camera pass-through ("does not offer a pass-through function" — physical flip-up only); it lists the US price as $1,899 and states Shiftall deliberately declines to publish FOV. Road to VR (Oct 11, 2024) corroborates the same model, the 3,552 x 3,840 per-eye resolution, 90 Hz, SteamVR base-station tracking, PC VR nature, the $1,899 price ("$1,900" in prose), and the February–March 2025 shipping window. fov_deg and storage_gb are null because neither fetched page states them (FOV is intentionally withheld; the PC-tethered headset has no onboard storage).

products.name: Play For Dream MR
products.priceNote: Manufacturer store pfdm.ai/products/mr-headset lists the 'MR Headset' at $1,999.00 USD for the 512 GB configuration (the only config offered, shown Sold out). UploadVR's launch coverage reported Kickstarter retail of $2,000 (512 GB) and $2,300 (1 TB).

specs.tracking: inside-out (outward tracking cameras + depth camera + eye tracking)

products.provenance: Manufacturer store page pfdm.ai/products/mr-headset lists the 'MR Headset' at $1,999.00 USD (512 GB, the only configuration offered, shown Sold out); its SPECS section states Micro-OLED single-eye resolution 3840x3552, 90 Hz refresh, pancake lenses at 103° FOV, total weight 650g including battery, 512 GB storage, a Color Passthrough Camera plus outward tracking, eye-tracking and depth cameras (inside-out), on Snapdragon XR2+ Gen 2. The Ghost Howls dated hands-on (Sept 11, 2025) independently lists the identical spec sheet — 3840×3552 per eye, 90 Hz, 103° FOV, 650g, 512 GB, Snapdragon XR2+ Gen 2 — confirming this is the exact Play For Dream MR standalone headset (distinct from the company's separate 'VR Headset'), and UploadVR's launch coverage corroborates the $2,000/512 GB retail and the 3840×3552 BOE micro-OLED panels. No single verbatim commercial-availability month appears on the fetched pages (global shipping was cited as starting around December with rollout through 2025), so release and releaseDate are left null.

products.name: HTC Vive Pro 2
products.priceNote: Road to VR launch review (June 1, 2021) lists "$800 for the headset by itself or $1,400 full kit price" (table: Headset Only $800, Full Kit $1,400). priceUsd uses the headset-only figure, consistent with other PC-tethered headsets in this catalog; base stations and controllers sold separately. Headset now discontinued.
products.provenance: HTC's official VIVE Pro 2 spec page confirms this exact model (Vive Pro 2, marketed as 5K, successor to the Vive Pro): 2448×2448 pixels per eye dual RGB low-persistence LCD, 90/120 Hz refresh, up to 120° horizontal field of view, and SteamVR Tracking V2.0 requiring external base stations — connected via DisplayPort 1.2 + USB 3.0, so it is PC-tethered (not standalone) with no internal storage. Road to VR's dated launch review (June 1, 2021) corroborates the same 2,448×2,448 per-eye LCD, 90Hz/120Hz, 120° horizontal FOV, SteamVR external-beacon tracking, "2x RGB" on-board cameras and "Pass-through view: Yes", and states the US price as "$800 for the headset by itself or $1,400 full kit." Wikipedia adds it was unveiled May 11, 2021 with the Full Kit shipping October 2021; the headset-only version reviewed here became available June 2021. No fetched page states headset weight verbatim, so weight_g is null.
